Pricing and access

No standalone plan, no free tier. Eligible: SuperGrok Plus/Heavy, Cursor Pro+ ($60), Ultra ($200), Teams ($40/user). Weekly usage included; on-demand extra.

All eight are free and open source. Variable costs: model API calls, a VPS or local Docker host, optional paid sandboxes (E2B, Daytona, Box), optional managed services (Nous Portal, openhuman subscription), and ElevenLabs for voice in openmausbot.

Model choice

Grok Bot runs on xAI's own models, and xAI documents no way to substitute another.

Six of eight offer native model choice; buzz and paperclip delegate model selection to their connected agents. rakazo uses any provider via Pi or OpenRouter, openbot accepts any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and openclaw works with any hosted or local provider. [...] What does Grok Bot cost and is there a free tier?

No free tier, no standalone plan. Eligible plans are SuperGrok Plus and Heavy, Cursor Pro+ ($60/mo), Cursor Ultra ($200/mo), and Cursor Teams ($40/user/mo); Cursor's pricing page also marks Grok Bot on its $20 Pro plan, so check there for the latest. xAI's docs show the subscription includes weekly Grok Bot usage; on-demand usage bills by model and token cost on top. All eight alternatives are free and open source. Recurring costs depend on how you run them: model API calls, a VPS or Docker host, and optionally paid sandboxes, managed services, or voice APIs.

Which open source alternative gives each agent its own isolated computer? [...] rakazo, openmausbot, openhuman, and openbot: browser, terminal, and file access. hermes-agent: cloud browser via Nous Portal. paperclip orchestrates but does not itself provide compute. buzz is a workspace surface. openclaw has a browser tool on a local profile, enabled per agent.

Hosting and source

Closed source. Cloud-only on xAI/Cursor infrastructure. No self-hosting option and no documented export path for skills or routines you build.

All eight are open source. Seven self-host via Docker or a native installer. Licenses range from MIT and Apache-2.0 to GPL-3.0 (openhuman). None require xAI infrastructure and all expose their full source for audit.

## FAQ

Is Grok Bot free?

Only as a trial. Cursor's Grok Bot plans page, checked on 30 Sep 2026, describes the trial as a usage credit with a seven day window. After that you need a paid individual Cursor plan, Cursor Teams, or a linked individual SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, SuperGrok Heavy or X Premium+ account. SuperGrok Lite does not include it.

What is the best free alternative to Grok Bot?

OpenClaw for a personal assistant in your chat apps, Munder Difflin for a team of coding agents, and Hermes Agent for memory that learns. All three are free and open source and run on hardware you control, but you still pay for the AI model or use a subscription you already have. Meta Muse has a free hosted tier in the US and Canada.

Is Gemini Spark better than Grok Bot? [...] ## Is there a free or open source Grok Bot alternative? #

Yes: OpenClaw, Munder Difflin, Hermes Agent and NanoClaw are all free and open source. The software costs nothing, but a model still does. Munder Difflin drives the CLIs you already have, so the Claude or ChatGPT subscription you pay for today does the work.

The trade is setup and uptime: you need a machine that stays on, or a small server, and security becomes your job. Meta Muse is the only hosted pick with a free tier, and only in North America.

# Grok Bot Alternatives: 9 Picks, Hosted or on Your Computer

Grok Bot runs every Bot on one shared cloud computer in the US. Nine alternatives checked on 30 Sep 2026, from ChatGPT dots to open source agents you run.

MD Chaitanya Giri · · 8 min read Comparisons

The best Grok Bot alternatives are ChatGPT dots for another always on agent with its own cloud computer, Munder Difflin or OpenClaw for agents on your own computer, and Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark or Meta Muse if you live in those apps. Every pick was rechecked on vendor pages on 30 Sep 2026.

By Grok Bot we mean SpaceXAI’s agent app, hosted by Cursor, not the Grok chatbot on X.
